title: Author + implement PROP-NNN: analyst Mode 1 starvation guard for aging priority=low pending items
background:
Operator observation (2026-06-02 ~05:00 UTC): analyst's Mode 1 deep-attack singleton selection appears to starve priority=low items. Concrete evidence from current expansion-tracker:

  EXP-526 (priority=low, ISS-2361, WIN-023 1000-year band): added 2026-05-31T14:49Z — pending ~38h
  EXP-534 (priority=low, ISS-2370, WIN-066 carry-forward): added 2026-05-31T14:49Z — pending ~38h
  EXP-551 (priority=low, ISS-2416, §8b.3 steel-man relocation): added 2026-06-01T09:14Z — pending ~20h
  EXP-552 (priority=low, ISS-2417, §8b.3 globe-infrastructure relocation): added 2026-06-01T09:14Z — pending ~20h

Meanwhile EXP-556 (priority=medium, added 2026-06-02T00:00Z, only ~5h old) was picked and authored by Opus-analyst at 03:17Z. Analyst ran ~19 times between 2026-05-31T14:49Z and 2026-06-02T05:00Z; the 4 priority=low items were eligible (not baby-owned, not blocked_on, claimed_by=None) but never selected. The pattern: each cycle, new priority=medium items arrive and analyst picks them over the older priority=low backlog.

This is classic priority-starvation. Decider is keeping up fine (3 integrations in the 02:00Z run alone — EXP-530, EXP-505, EXP-554). The bottleneck is upstream of decider: analyst's Mode 1 selection ordering. The 4 priority=low EXPs may sit indefinitely as long as new priority=medium items keep arriving (which they do — about 1 medium-priority deep-attack per day from curmudgeon/decider routing).

Two of the 4 (EXP-551, EXP-552) are explicitly tagged in their `notes` field as consolidatable ('analyst may consolidate with sibling EXP-462 follow-ups') — so once the starvation is broken, throughput recovers further because they can bundle into one EXP.

operator_decision.rationale: Priority starvation is a real bug. Low priority should mean 'do this later' not 'never do this.' A guard that promotes any pending item older than ~24h to top-of-queue ensures fair drain without invalidating the priority signal for the first day.

requested_work: Step 1 — Read `monitor/prompts/reference/analyst-mode1-expansions.md` (the Mode 1 selection-logic reference) and `monitor/prompts/analyst.md` (the Mode 1 entrypoint that filters the tracker pending list). Locate the EXACT lines where pending-item selection ordering happens. The current ordering is implicit — appears to be by priority then by ID — and operator does not know the precise sort key without reading the code.

Step 2 — Author `monitor/tinker/proposals/PROP-NNN-analyst-mode1-starvation-guard.json` (next free PROP-NNN at time of authoring). Required sections: title, problem statement (cite this directive + the 4 concrete EXP examples), proposed fix (the selection-rule change), Q-OPs (open questions for operator if any — e.g., what threshold age: 24h vs 36h vs 48h?), verification_pattern (a grep that confirms the new selection logic is in the file), files_touched list, estimated_loc.

Step 3 — Operator pre-approves the following design directions; tinker should pick the cleanest:
  (a) Hard age threshold: if any pending item's age >= 24h, promote it to top-of-queue regardless of priority. Multiple aged items sort among themselves by age (oldest first).
  (b) Soft priority boost: items aged >24h get an effective +1 priority bump for selection purposes. Items aged >48h get +2.
  (c) Round-robin: alternate cycles between 'newest priority=medium+' and 'oldest pending regardless of priority'.
  Operator preference: (a) for simplicity, unless tinker's analysis surfaces a strong reason for (b) or (c).

Step 4 — Operator approves tinker self-apply per the PROP-070/072/073 pattern: tinker writes the proposal, then implements it in the SAME run if (a) operator approval embedded in this directive is sufficient, (b) the implementation is ≤30 lines, (c) verification_pattern passes. If tinker has Q-OPs that aren't pre-answered above, hold for operator review before implementing.

Step 5 — Validate with the 4 currently-stuck items: after the fix is in `monitor/prompts/...`, a manual analyst run on the next 2h cycle should pick EXP-526 (oldest priority=low) ahead of any new priority=medium arrivals. Document this expectation in the PROP file's 'post-deployment canary' section.

Step 6 — Lifecycle: flip PROP-NNN.json status='implemented' with implementation_commit + implementation_at + implementation_run recorded. Flip this directive to status='completed' with prop_id_implemented='PROP-NNN'.

Step 7 — Manually copy edited prompt files to FUSE so the next scheduled analyst run picks up the new logic (per the per-session FUSE staleness pattern; dome-mirror will propagate within ~1h but manual sync is the safe bootstrap path).
non_goals: Do NOT manually bump the 4 stuck items' priority from 'low' to 'medium' in the tracker — that treats the symptom not the cause. The starvation guard should naturally drain them on the next analyst run. (If operator wants both belt-and-suspenders, that's a separate manual action.)
Do NOT bump analyst's cadence (it's already 2h, plenty fast). The fix is selection ordering, not throughput.
Do NOT touch analyst-baby's selection logic in this proposal — baby has its own ordering rules and a different work surface. If similar starvation exists in baby's queue, that's a separate PROP-NNN.
Do NOT add a new priority level. Operate within the existing low/medium/high/critical scale.
Do NOT make this a blanket 'age-bumps-priority' rule for all agents — scope this to analyst Mode 1 deep-attack singleton selection only. Other agents have different pacing assumptions.

context_pointers.tracker_evidence: monitor/analyst/expansion-tracker.json — the 4 priority=low pending entries (EXP-526, EXP-534, EXP-551, EXP-552) all with claimed_at=null and created_at >= 20h ago
context_pointers.analyst_selection_logic: monitor/prompts/analyst.md (Mode 1 entrypoint + dispatcher filter) and monitor/prompts/reference/analyst-mode1-expansions.md (the actual selection-ordering reference)
context_pointers.successful_recent_authorings_today: EXP-556 (priority=medium, ISS-2443) authored 03:17Z; EXP-557 (priority=?, baby-batch) authored 03:35Z — both newer than the stuck 4
context_pointers.decider_is_not_the_bottleneck: decider-2026-06-02T02-00 summary (monitor/decisions/latest-decider-summary.txt) shows 3 integrations in that run alone — EXP-530, EXP-505, EXP-554. Throughput is fine downstream of the stuck queue.
context_pointers.consolidation_opportunity: EXP-551 and EXP-552 are tagged in their notes field 'analyst may consolidate with sibling EXP-462 follow-ups' — once selection-ordering unsticks them, they can merge into one EXP, further speeding drain.
context_pointers.related_prior_propsals: PROP-029 (route-to-analyst on PROP-034 split — minor/moderate orphans to baby), PROP-034 (analyst/baby Phase 1 split). Neither addresses priority-starvation within the items that DO remain in Opus-analyst's queue.

expected_output: (1) monitor/tinker/proposals/PROP-NNN-analyst-mode1-starvation-guard.json with status='implemented' (or 'design-pending-operator-review' if tinker found Q-OPs not pre-answered above). (2) If implemented: a small edit to monitor/prompts/reference/analyst-mode1-expansions.md (or analyst.md, depending on where the selection logic lives) adding the age-threshold guard. (3) This directive flipped to status='completed' with prop_id_implemented set. (4) FUSE-synced prompt edits so the next analyst run uses the new logic.
estimated_effort: ~30-45 min Opus. Proposal authoring (~15 min), implementation (~15 min, expect ~10-line code/prose change), validation + lifecycle flips (~10 min).
priority_note: MEDIUM — not blocking anything urgent, but the 4 stuck EXPs represent ~38h of accumulating drag on the review's coverage and quality. Each day this isn't fixed, more low-priority items accumulate the same way. Worth shipping in the next 1-2 tinker runs.
